tool: Example chat helper (an invented tool, for illustration only)
purpose: Drafting plain-language versions of general clinic handouts, never for questions about one person
reviewed_by: CF nurse, dietitian, social worker, parent representative, adult with CF

rows.question: Who built it, and were people with CF lived experience and CF clinicians involved?
rows.found: The vendor page names a clinical advisor; it says nothing about people with lived experience.

rows.question: What data trained it, and how well does it represent people with CF of different ages, languages, regions and access?
What do the terms say about storing and reusing chats?
rows.found: The terms say chats are kept and may be used to improve the service unless the account owner turns this off.
rows.where: document: terms of service, section on data, read 2026-10-08

rows.question: How are errors and made-up content watched for, and who can see the reports?
rows.found: In our test, one of five invented handout rewrites changed a number; nothing in the tool warned us.

rows.question: What happens when it is wrong, and how do we stop using it?

red_flags.note: Sign-up asks for an email only.
The terms state it, in a long section.

decision.use_for: drafting rewrites of general handouts that contain no personal information
checks: A staff member compares every number, name and rule with the original before use
Chat history setting turned off, and checked again each quarter
Review again in six months or after any change to the tool
decision.decided_by: CF nurse lead and parent representative, after the group discussion
